text: 🍿 The Exorcist: Martyrs puts Scarlett Johansson in the devil's crosshairs 📆 Release: March 12, 2027 🎭 Genre: #Horror · #Thriller ✈️ Add to watchlist Mike Flanagan is finally getting his Exorcist, and /Film says the trailer swerves from the franchise's usual dread. Scarlett Johansson plays an NYPD detective chasing a killer who calls himself Father Sunday. That makes it a procedural first and a possession story second. It's a smart way in after sequels that kept trying to out-scare Friedkin. Flanagan has the tools, from the chamber-piece tension of 'Hush' to a gift for grief and faith. If the film honors the ritual and doesn't treat it as a gimmick, this could be the best thing the series has done in decades.

🎬 Nick Fury skips Doomsday and waits for Secret Wars Samuel L. Jackson says he's not in 'Avengers: Doomsday'. His next Marvel movie is the one after it, which means Fury sits out the X-Men reunion and the Evans and Hemsworth comeback party. That's a smart call. Fury has been a cameo with an eyepatch since the 2008 post-credits scene, and 'Secret Invasion' did him no favors. Saving him for a Battleworld pile-up gives him a reason to show up again. 'Avengers: Secret Wars' is set for December 17, 2027, with no plot details yet.

🍿 Carrie ends with a door open to a bigger King world /Film argues that Mike Flanagan has quietly soft-launched a second King universe. His 'Carrie' moves the story to the social media era and writes the bullies as people, not cartoons. Then it frames Carrie White as one link in a long line of psychic women. That's the smart part. A shared universe built on a lineage of powers beats stitching Easter eggs together, which is how 'The Dark Tower' (2017) sank. Flanagan already proved with 'Doctor Sleep' (2019) that he can honor King and still go his own way. Eight episodes on Prime Video, with Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan. Flanagan's dream is three seasons, and no second season is confirmed yet. ✈️ Add to watchlist
